nodes.notes: Serves an n8n-hosted form (From, Subject, Receivedat). Each submission becomes one execution.

nodes.name: Normalize Email Payload
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Normalize incoming email records to a stable schema Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Route by Work Type
nodes.notes: Routes each item to one of 4 lanes: standard, priority, vip + fallback. Watch out: Unmatched items go to the fallback output; without one they are silently dropped.

nodes.name: Process 'standard' → Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Email Tracker', matched on messageId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack (#inbox-ops) — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Email Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Merge Routed Work
nodes.notes: Rejoins 4 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Load Previous Snapshot
nodes.notes: Reads every row from 'Email Tracker' — the read side of the store, e.g. for a digest or a downstream sync. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Compute Drift vs Snapshot
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Compare current metrics with the previous snapshot Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

# Capture applications: Google Sheets & Slack, form

**Pattern:** Form Intake · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Form

## Overview

Starts when the form is submitted, and covers inbox-triage work end to end across Google Sheets, Slack, Notion and Gmail.

It moves through 17 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. New Email Form Submission
2. Normalize Email Payload
3. Route by Work Type
4. Process 'standard' → Google Sheets
5. Fast-Track 'priority' + Alert
6. Fast-Track 'vip' + Alert
7. Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
8. Merge Routed Work
9. Load Previous Snapshot
10. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
11. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
12. Archive Row Snapshot
13. Enrich with Reference Data
14. Fold In Enrichment Fields
15. Summarize Run Stats
16. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
17. Send Summary to Gmail

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing inbox-triage work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

New Email Form Submission → Normalize Email Payload → Route by Work Type → Process 'standard' → Google Sheets → Fast-Track 'priority' + Alert → Fast-Track 'vip' + Alert → Hold Unknown Types (DLQ) → Merge Routed Work → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Gmail → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Slack aligned by hand for inbox triage
- Intake checked for completeness before it is stored in Google Sheets, for inbox triage
- Inbox triage work where "Normalize Email Payload" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Inbox triage work that only reaches Google Sheets when a form is submitted, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Slack in step for inbox triage, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Google Sheets or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 20 nodes in this inbox-triage build
- Branches rejoin before Google Sheets, so a inbox-triage run reports once rather than 20 times
- Fans the same result out to Notion in the same run, for inbox triage
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 20 nodes for inbox triage before wiring Google Sheets

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account; Notion integration token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Unrecognized work types are parked in a dead-letter lane instead of erroring the whole run or silently dropping the item — new event kinds will show up eventually, and this is where you'd notice one without losing it. One kind is deliberately routed through a sub-workflow to show how heavier per-type logic can be extracted without touching this router at all.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Send a work-type value that matches no switch rule and confirm it lands in the dead-letter branch.
2. Add a new work type and its own handling branch.
3. Replace the direct-write branch with a sub-workflow call, matching the pattern already used for the first kind.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).
_Gotcha:_ Add n8n's OAuth redirect URL exactly as shown in the credential, or the consent loop fails.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your inbox triage process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- Gmail: request the narrowest send/read scope the nodes need — full mailbox access is rarely required.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
inbox-triage payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
